title: The prediction and outcome log: every row a model in use scores, and its true outcome, joined by a hashed key
request: Build package 34.9 of phase 10 (layer 6, Learn): versioned contracts PredictionRecord and OutcomeRecord in dclab_core, registered like the others, and the exported scoring service logging every /predict and /predict/csv to predictions.jsonl and taking POST /outcome; a CORE_INTEGRATION section for the main product, which runs customer models. Never a cell value in a record.
spec: dclab_core.serving: PredictionRecord v1 (model id and version, batch and position, the key as a 32-hex salted hash, task, score, class by index, decision as a code, threshold, time) and OutcomeRecord v1 (key, outcome coded as the model predicts it, known_at, recorded_at); key_hash (HMAC-SHA-256), new_key, code_outcome, read_log, join. The service template gains serve_log.py (Flask-free logic, appends under a lock) and thin routes in app.py; the export writes model_id, model_version (a fingerprint of model.pkl) and the binary target's negative label into model.json, copies serve_log.py, sets DCLAB_SERVICE_LOG_DIR=/logs in the image, keeps *.jsonl out of it, and its generated tests check a prediction joins its outcome.
plan: read the plan section, the service export and its template, how contracts are registered
write failing tests: the core contracts, and an end-to-end test through the exported service
build dclab_core/serving.py and register it (contracts import, CONTRACT_ADAPTERS reason, schemas, 0.106.0)
wire the service: serve_log.py, app.py routes, export meta and README
CHANGELOG, CORE_INTEGRATION section, a wheel-check smoke call
wheel check, the reviewer, fixes with tests

decisions.decision: The key is always a salted hash (HMAC with a secret the service holds), and the contract enforces 32 hex characters
decisions.why: a caller's key is usually an order or customer id, a cell value; a plain hash of a guessable id can be reversed by trying them all, a keyed one cannot without the secret

decisions.decision: A caller with no key column gets a random key per row back with its prediction
decisions.why: the outcome must be postable later; a random number is no value of the table

decisions.decision: The route logic lives in a Flask-free serve_log.py; app.py stays thin
decisions.why: Flask is in no environment of the repository; the logic is tested directly, and the routes through a small stand-in for Flask in an isolated Python

decisions.decision: Outcomes are coded as the model predicts them (binary 1/0, multiclass index, regression value); a value that is neither label is refused
decisions.why: a typo read as a negative would silently bias live performance and a retrain

decisions.decision: Log keys use DCLAB_LOG_KEY, falling back to the export's DCLAB_SERVICE_KEY
decisions.why: each export makes a new service key; outcomes arrive after a retrain and must still join the earlier model's predictions

decisions.decision: No main-product table maps onto the records; conformance lists them as library output with the reason
decisions.why: the field lists read at the main product's commit have no serving tables; the guide says how it should store them

decisions.decision: check-quick not run during the day
decisions.why: the owner's rule: daytime runs only the tests proving the change, gates run nightly and alone; the shared tree also held another session's unfinished data_value contract, which fails the schema tests and the wheel check's conformance call

change: dclab_core/serving.py (new); dclab_core/contracts.py (import line); dclab_core/adapters/conformance.py (two reasons); dclab_core/__init__.py, pyproject.toml (0.106.0); dclab_core/CHANGELOG.md; dclab_core/schemas/prediction_record.json, outcome_record.json and their baselines; dclab_rnd/studio/service_template/serve_log.py (new), app.py; dclab_rnd/studio/service.py (meta, copy, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, README, generated tests); scripts/core_wheel_check.py (smoke); docs/guides/CORE_INTEGRATION.md (section); tests/test_core_serving.py (new); tests/test_service_export.py (end-to-end test).

findings.defect: a retrain cut outcomes off from older predictions
findings.scenario: order 123 scored Monday under export key 1; the project re-exported Tuesday (new key 2); the outcome posted Wednesday is hashed with key 2 and never joins, while /outcome answers recorded: 1
findings.cause: keys were hashed with the export's service key, which each export makes anew
findings.fix: a log key DCLAB_LOG_KEY that outlives exports, documented in the README
findings.impact: every outcome arriving after a redeploy lost to monitoring and retraining
alternatives: keep the secret in a file beside the logs (whoever holds the logs then holds the secret)
findings.open: without DCLAB_LOG_KEY set, the fallback still changes per export: the README says to set it

findings.defect: a float-written key in a CSV never joined its JSON outcome
findings.scenario: a CSV with order_id 470000166.0 (pandas or Excel writing a float column) read as text, the outcome posted with 470000166: two hashes
findings.cause: _text normalised float objects only, not their text
findings.fix: a text of the form digits.0 is read as its integer; '007' stays '007'
findings.impact: silent loss of outcomes for CSV callers

findings.defect: one torn line made a whole log unreadable
findings.scenario: a monitor reads predictions.jsonl during a large write, or a worker is killed mid-line and the next batch lands on the same line
findings.cause: read_log raised on the first bad line; the writer did not close a torn line
findings.fix: read_log skips lines that are not JSON (a JSON line that is not the contract still raises); the writer starts on a new line when the file does not end in one
findings.impact: monitoring and retrain blocked by one crash

findings.defect: /outcome accepted a key that cannot be a row key
findings.fix: key_hash refuses anything but text or a number (a bool too)

findings.defect: binary 1/0 was accepted when it was not one of the model's labels
findings.scenario: labels 1 and 2 (positive 2): an outcome 0 was read as the negative
findings.cause: the plain 1/0 map applied whatever the labels
findings.fix: 1/0 and true/false only when the negative label is unknown or the labels are themselves those
findings.impact: a typo read as a negative

findings.defect: some bad bodies answered 500 instead of 400
findings.cause: the key column name and the rows were not checked before use
findings.fix: a key column must be text and rows an object or a list of objects, else Refused (400)

findings.defect: the log's row keys changed with every export
findings.scenario: a model retrained and exported again: an outcome posted to the new export never joined a prediction the last one logged
findings.cause: without DCLAB_LOG_KEY the log hashed keys with the export's own key, which is new each time, and DCLab gave no stable key
findings.fix: one log key per project, made once and kept beside the project in a file the store and the testers' kit skip by its name; every export returns it beside its own key and the README's run line passes it
findings.test: tests/test_service_export.py (two exports, one log key, never in an export or a record)
findings.impact: monitoring with outcomes and a retrain lost the rows of every earlier export
alternatives: refuse to log without DCLAB_LOG_KEY (a service that fails by default)
a fixed default key (a dictionary of hashed ids anyone could rebuild)

findings.defect: the stable log key was never made on PostgreSQL
findings.scenario: DCLAB_DATABASE_URL set (make dev, the cloud): two exports returned no log key while the README promised one
findings.cause: the key's folder came from store.directory, which only the file store has; the error was caught and the key silently skipped
findings.fix: the folder comes from export_dir, which both backends have and both delete with the project
findings.impact: logs that never join across exports on every deployed workspace
alternatives: a secrets_dir method on the storage protocol

findings.defect: the key file was briefly readable by others, and two first exports could race
findings.scenario: the file written with the default mode, then made private; two exports at once each writing a different key
findings.cause: write then chmod, no exclusive create
findings.fix: the folder owner-only, the file created owner-only and exclusively; the loser of a race reads the winner's key; a short key is made again
findings.impact: a key another local user could read; a first export whose logs never join

findings.defect: the challenge solver raised NameError after the log key moved to one per project
findings.scenario: an approved challenge result exports its service: challenge/__init__.py still returned `key`, the variable 001427a9 removed when export() began returning the keys in a dict, so every approved challenge failed
findings.cause: the change renamed a local in export()'s callers but the tests run for it (test_service_export) never reached the challenge path, and the full gate was owed
findings.fix: service_key reads exported["key"] (fixed by the A7 session in 4393e95b, found by its gate)

measurements.name: tests.test_core_serving and tests.test_service_export
measurements.gate: a batch scored and its outcomes posted join by key; no input value in either log (the plan's Done when)
measurements.result: 13 tests pass (177 s): 40 JSON rows and 30 CSV rows keyed by order_id plus 2 with made-up keys scored, 71 outcomes posted, a bad outcome refused with nothing recorded; the logs join on all 71 keys with the right outcomes; no order id, text value or the service key in either log
limits: numeric input values are not searched for in the logs; the contract's fields (extra=forbid, a 32-hex key, a code-only decision) rule them out instead

measurements.name: the export's generated tests under real Flask 3.1.3
measurements.gate: the generated tests/test_service.py of an export pass under the real framework
measurements.result: 4 passed (the reviewer, in a scratch venv; Flask is in no environment of the repository)

measurements.name: make core-wheel-check
measurements.gate: the wheel builds, installs in a clean Python 3.12 and its smoke calls pass, serving included
measurements.result: passed on a copy without another session's unfinished data_value (dclab-core 0.106.0); in the shared tree it failed only on data_value's missing conformance reason at that time
limits: not rerun in the shared tree once data_value was finished

measurements.name: make check-quick
measurements.gate: the package gate passes on the affected files
measurements.result: not run: the owner's daytime rule (only the tests proving the change; gates nightly and alone); a first run was stopped before the reviewer's fixes
measurements.next: the nightly gate, once the other sessions' packages in the tree are finished

outcome: The contracts and the working reference exist; a batch scored and its outcomes posted join by key, and no input value is in either log (tested). 34.10 and 34.11 can read the logs through serving.read_log and serving.join.
lessons: A keyed hash's secret must outlive the thing that issues it when records written under it are joined later
Every place a key or a label is normalised must treat the CSV form of a float the same as the number
An append-only log needs a reader that survives a torn line and a writer that never glues onto one
A permissive fallback in outcome coding (1/0) becomes a silent mislabel when the labels are other numbers
A change that renames what a function returns must search every caller, and the gate that runs every test is owed until it runs
risks: Without DCLAB_LOG_KEY set, outcomes posted after a re-export do not join (documented, not enforced)
The logs grow without rotation; 34.10 should read them incrementally
Concurrency rests on fcntl locks on a local file system; a network volume may not honour them
